dedupe_keys.name: heat plan denmark 2021 a climate neutral heat supply for 2030 and 2045 aalborg university sustainable energy planning research group

description: This case study is Heat Plan Denmark 2021, a proposal from Aalborg University's Sustainable Energy Planning Research Group for how the Danish heating sector can be transformed to meet the 70% emission reduction target for 2030 and climate neutrality by 2050, modelled for 2030 (VPDK-30) and 2045 (VPDK-45). It concludes that available technologies suffice: 36 to 40% energy savings in buildings, district heating expanded by 63 to 70% as natural gas and oil boilers are shut down, individual heat pumps outside district heating areas, and 4th generation district heating with lower temperatures that makes best use of geothermal energy, surplus heat, large heat pumps and heat storage. It reports savings of more than 1.1 to 1.3 billion kroner and up to 2 TWh of biomass avoided. Access: free to read on the university research portal, which lists seven outputs and a dataset, with Danish-language reports and mapping tools at the project's own site; no licence is stated. Coverage is national. Caveats: only the project summary was read, and the linked reports and dataset were not opened. It suits adaptation planning and capacity planning studies of national heat transitions, and no directly related records are catalogued yet.

outcomes: The plan proposes that the Danish heating sector reach the 2030 and 2045 targets through 36 to 40% energy savings in the building stock, district heating expansion of 63 to 70% as gas and oil boilers close, individual heat pumps outside district heating areas, and a move to 4th generation district heating with lower temperatures, geothermal, surplus heat, large heat pumps and heat storage. It reports savings of more than 1.1 to 1.3 billion kroner for 36% energy savings and up to 2 TWh of biomass spared.
